title: Sequenced standby warmup with priority demotion playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and executable checklist for active->passive regional promotions that prioritizes user-visible traffic as the standby warms up. This ticket delivers: (1) a sequenced warmup procedure for passive regions that incrementally enables services, (2) a priority-demotion policy for non-critical flows (background jobs, batch ingest) to free capacity during warmup, (3) circuit-breaker tuning guidance to avoid cascading failovers, and (4) an automated backup/restore validation harness for KV stores and token caches used during switchover. The goal is to enable predictable, repeatable failovers with verifiable data integrity and SLO preservation for high-priority routes.
acceptance_criteria: A step-by-step runbook exists that operators can follow to perform a sequenced passive->active promotion with less than 5% user-facing error increase for critical routes
Automated priority-demotion policy applied during drills that reduces background jobs to <20% of normal throughput while preserving critical traffic
Circuit-breaker and throttling defaults for promotions documented and captured in runtime-1.22-configs
Backup/restore validation harness successfully restores a representative KV snapshot to standby region and verifies key-level checksum and tokenstore consistency
Two scheduled failover drills executed in staging and one in a low-risk prod window with post-mortem and checklist updates
runbook_steps: Pre-checks: validate snapshot cadence, last KV checkpoint age < 10m, tokenstore replication health green, SLO burn-rate baseline captured
Quiesce non-essential writers: mark background job fleet to 'drill-mode', drain long-running jobs using priority-demotion policy
Restore snapshot to standby VMs/GKE nodes using dr-restore-harness (link to CI job)
Warm caches: preload top-5% prefix KV reads and prime model KV caches with recent session hotkeys
Enable L7 route gating: gradually open critical route by 10% increments with 2m observation windows and circuit-breaker thresholds set to 5xx-rate > 1% triggers rollback
Monitor SLOs and token latency: if p99 request latency increases >30% or error-rate > baseline thresholds, pause and run targeted mitigations
Enable non-critical flows at demoted priority only after critical route SLOs stabilize for 10 minutes
Post-cutover reconciliation: run snapshot-compare tool for KV namespaces and tokenstore diff, surface mismatches to oncall and block full promotion until reconciled
Finalize: mark new region active, update routing control-plane, rotate any ephemeral keys, and capture drill artifacts
rollback_criteria: Any sustained p50/p95 latency regression beyond defined runway (p95 > baseline + 40%)
Error-rate for critical routes exceeds 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive 2-minute windows
KV checksum mismatches > 0.1% of keys after automatic reconciliation
Circuit-breakers trip for more than 5 independent upstream services
Manual operator judgement: ops lead flags rollback during checklist clearance
metrics_and_dashboards: SLOs to monitor: critical-route availability (99.95), p95 latency, user-error-rate
Runbook dashboard: promotion-phase timeline, percent of traffic shifted, background-job throughput
KV integrity dashboard: snapshot age, restored-key-count, checksum-diff-rate
Circuit-breaker dashboard: trips per minute, downstream-error amplification, fallback rates
